meta.heading: Round 5: the main way around
meta.intro: You liked the canvas with its timeline, a calendar planner that folds open, and notes in a side strip. Round 5 tries three ways to hold those together, in the coloured-paper style you asked for. M1 (the encrypted core) is being built meanwhile.

r5-nav.title: Three ways to get around Shiftbook
body: All three keep what you liked: the **notes strip** is always on the right (jot, meeting or daily), the **canvas** is a mode you can switch any view into, and the **planner** folds open by week, month and year. What changes is the main way you move around. There's no menu list in any of them.
They're in the coloured-paper style from your canvas note: real colour per project, a light paper grain and soft edges, without tape, torn edges or tilted cards. Every one is clickable.

figures.caption: **1 · Zoom through time.** The calendar is the menu. Year → month → week → day, each one zooming in from what you clicked, and a day folds open in place. Calendar/Canvas switches how the same days are shown.
**2 · Time ribbon.** A strip of days along the top, each a little bar of coloured hours. Pick a day or drag across a range, and it folds open below as a plan, a canvas or its notes.

**3 · The desk.** Home is a desk with four things on it: this week, the Inbox, Notes and the Map. Click one and it opens to fill the desk; Back puts it down. You find things by where they sit, not by a list.

questions.legend: Which one should be THE way around?

options.why: Time is what Shiftbook is about, so time is the menu. One control (Year · Month · Week · Day) and you always know where you are.
Always shows the last few weeks at a glance; good for spotting empty days before a timesheet.
Most unusual; good if you remember things by place.
Say which parts in the box, e.g. Zoom with the ribbon as its week bar.

questions.legend: What made you pick it, or what's still missing? (optional)
questions.placeholder: e.g. 1, but I want the ribbon always visible at the top

r5-nav.pick: 1 · Zoom. If you like the ribbon's at-a-glance bars, they could sit above the week view.

r5-canvas.title: The canvas in coloured paper
body: More colour, a paper feel, and no clichés. Each card has a soft grain and a coloured top edge for its project; project areas are tinted in the same colour; the project card itself is solid colour so it reads as the anchor. A dashed coral outline marks a scrap still waiting in the Inbox.

figures.caption: Drag cards and try **Arrange as timeline** again.

options.why: e.g. tint whole cards, not just the edge.
Keep colour to the edges only.

r5-canvas.pick: Yes. This becomes the starting style for the real screens.

r5-privacy.title: "Include the text as well": which did you mean?
body: On the screenshot card you wrote that protection should include the text as well. I want to get this right, because the two readings pull in opposite directions.

options.why: While protected, copy and drag-out are blocked as well; the timed allow button unlocks both. Note this also blocks copying hours or notes into your timesheet until you press it.
A visible line such as 'Screenshots allowed · 8:42 left', so you always know the state.

r5-privacy.pick: Your call. If it's copying, I'd keep the timesheet's Copy button working even while protected, since copying is the whole point there.

r5-rules.title: How Shiftbook reads what you type: choices to check
body: The first half of M1 is done: the rules for hours, weeks, projects, recurring work, tickets and timesheet totals, with 88 tests. Where the spec didn't say, I made a choice. These are the ones you'd notice.

head: If you…
Shiftbook does
rows: type a plain number like `8` or `45`
Up to 24 means hours (`8` = 8 h). Above 24 means minutes (`45` = 45 min).
All mean 90 minutes. Odd decimals round to the nearest minute.
type `1:75` or `1h 75m`
Says it doesn't understand, rather than guessing.
log 0 hours
Allowed, e.g. for "Mark done" on a recurring item with no time spent. Max 24 h per entry.
set "Warn days before" to blank or 0
Blank means 30 days. 0 means warn only on the due day.
add 1 month to 31 January
You get the last day of February (28 or 29).
give a project an estimate of 0
Treated as no estimate: no % used, never "Over budget".
paste `INC1, inc1, INC2`
Two tickets, since duplicates are ignored regardless of capitals. Up to 100 per entry.
delete an entry
It stops counting everywhere (totals, last done), but can be restored.
rename the Done or Blocked status
Not allowed, because the alerts depend on those two words. Every other list value can be renamed or hidden.

bullets: **Default lists** (all editable): categories Troubleshooting, Maintenance, Support / Tickets, Meetings, Project work, Documentation, Training, Admin, Travel. Statuses Not started, In progress, Waiting, Blocked, Done. Priorities Low, Medium, High, Urgent. Ten repeat frequencies from Daily to Every 3 years. No timesheet codes; you add your own.

questions.legend: A plain number with no unit

options.why: `8` is a workday, `45` is a meeting. Both read as you'd mean them.
`45` would be refused as too many hours.
Say which row in the note.

r5-rules.pick: Keep them all. The hours rule is the one most worth a second look.
